definitions: Used to introduce a statement that presents a balanced or mitigating perspective.
Used to acknowledge a valid point from an opposing view or to qualify a previous statement.
examples: I was annoyed, but to be fair, she did apologize.
The movie wasn't great, but to be fair, the acting was good.
He's often late, but to be fair, he has a long commute.
synonyms: to give credit where credit is due
